harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired and persisted the status service on node1. It runs as statusd, restricts access to statusd/status-readers, validates requests, preserves the supplied document, and recovered successfully after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Provisioned statusd, status-reader, outsider, and status-readers with correct membership.
Updated server.py for exact `STATUS\n` handling and `ERROR\n` responses.
Secured the socket as statusd:status-readers mode 0660 and protected its runtime directory.
Added and enabled a legacy-compatible SysV service.
Restarted node1 and verified a changed boot identity plus complete recovery.
Preserved Ubuntu 7.10, kernel 2.6.22-14-generic, and the status document checksum 992740401/24 bytes.

evidence.requirement: Service owner and role-based access boundary
evidence.summary: The process and socket use statusd/status-readers; status-reader succeeds while outsider receives Permission denied, including after reboot.

evidence.requirement: STATUS request returns the supplied document; invalid requests return an error
evidence.summary:
Owner and reader received `branch=west
state=ready
`; invalid requests received `ERROR
`.
Checksum remained 992740401 with a length of 24 bytes before changes, after repair, and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Persistent operation on the legacy platform
evidence.summary: SysV startup was enabled and the service automatically returned after reboot on unchanged Ubuntu 7.10/kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.

Healthy baseline used boot ID bed3c988-4d79-467e-92e8-e0c7211252f9; reboot was acknowledged; the recovered boot ID changed to afd66d4f-6c7e-4fbd-8a78-778d822fb0e5; service, identities, permissions, document, protocol, and access controls all recovered.
